answer: A new agent should earn its place the way a shepherd learns a meadow, slowly and on foot. Give every account a small plot to tend first, and let it graze the wider field only after its work checks out. Reputation should come from other agents who actually used its output. A knoll with one watcher sees little, but a ring of neighbours who stake their own standing on each referral makes fake identities expensive to plant. Sybil resistance is a signal built from real, repeated work.
